audit_findings.title: The equity-interest rail may fail because current interest is capitalized rather than expensed
audit_findings.magnitude: $83.6 million FY2025 timing gap between $241.7 million incurred and $158.1 million charged to cost of sales; full valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If the inventory or reinvestment adjustment does not capture capitalized interest, anchor OE omits a current financing cost that belongs to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company’s active inventory exceeded its debt level, and all interest incurred was capitalized to inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting deferral is demonstrated, but an OE error is not: the record does not show whether the $83.6 million increase in capitalized interest was deducted through working capital or another adjustment. The same gap was $74.4 million for the first nine months of FY2026, so the issue is recurring, but its cumulative effect cannot be established without the OE workpapers.
audit_findings.action: Trace incurred interest, cost-of-sales amortization, capitalized-interest balances and inventory adjustments for every OE year; rerun the valuation after deducting any amount not otherwise captured exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The full cash addback may include operating liquidity rather than distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,078.7 million, equal to $7.29 per diluted share and 5.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash dollar-for-dollar even though cash required for operations, collateral, regulation or subsidiary liquidity is not distributable surplus.
audit_findings.evidence: We are maintaining significant homebuilding cash balances and liquidity to support the scale and level of activity in our business and to provide flexibility to adjust to changing market conditions and opportunities.
audit_findings.explanation: The full addback is demonstrated, while full distributability is not. Management expressly maintains significant liquidity for operations, and the balance includes cash in homebuilding, rental, Forestar and financial-services entities. The amount is large enough to materially change the bridge and the margin-of-safety price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash by entity and purpose; deduct closing proceeds in transit, captive-insurance funding, pledged or regulatory balances, covenant minimums and ordinary seasonal liquidity, then rerun all scenarios using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Forestar consolidation can mix a 100% numerator or cash balance with DHI's 62% economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $150.1 million of June 2026 Forestar cash attributable to the 38% noncontrolling interest; OE-adjustment exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Using 100% of Forestar cash or positive operating results overstates DHI value, while using 100% of Forestar reinvestment or other negative adjustments can understate it.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, the Company owns a 62 % controlling interest in Forestar Group Inc. (Forestar) and therefore is required to consolidate 100% of Forestar within its consolidated financial statements, and the 38 % interest the Company does not own is accounted for as noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: A bridge mismatch is demonstrated: 38% of Forestar's $394.9 million cash, or $150.1 million, is not economically owned by DHI shareholders, equal to about $0.53 per diluted share and 0.4% of base equity value. That cash error alone is not material, but the record does not establish whether the OE numerator and all reinvestment adjustments were consistently attributed, so the total effect remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE from net income attributable to D.R. Horton, attribute each Forestar noncash and reinvestment adjustment at 62%, remove $150.1 million of NCI-owned cash from the bridge, and rerun if the combined correction is material.

audit_findings.title: The portfolio-income purge could remove operating mortgage or rental income
audit_findings.magnitude: $204.4 million of FY2025 operating other-income categories at risk, comprising $88.9 million from financial services and $115.5 million from rental; exact amount purged unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing mortgage-loan interest or rental income lowers anchor OE even though those earnings arise from businesses included in the valuation perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income, net of other expense, included in our financial services operations consists primarily of the interest income of our mortgage subsidiary.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that mortgage interest and rental income are operating components of other income. The valuation record does not identify what was actually purged, but the filed categories potentially affected total 8.0% of anchor OE. If all $204.4 million were restored and capitalized using the base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio, the computed effect would be about $2.87 billion or $10.07 per share, approximately the entire gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Produce the purge ledger by segment and account; retain mortgage-loan interest, rental income and other operating ancillary income, remove only returns on genuinely excess cash or securities, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor contains a tax benefit that is legislated to expire
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.5 million, equal to 1.6% of anchor OE and approximately $555 million or $1.95 per share under the base valuation multiple
audit_findings.mechanism: An unadjusted temporary tax credit raises anchor OE and is then grown into forecast periods after the credit expires.
audit_findings.evidence: The new law terminates the energy efficient home tax credit for homes closing after June 30, 2026 and enacts certain other tax provisions that will impact our financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the credit was normalized out is unresolved, but the maximum identified error is concretely bounded. Removing $39.5 million would reduce the computed base value from $132.55 to about $130.60 per share, still below the $142.75 market price, and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the anchor's tax reconciliation; if the benefit remains, remove $39.5 million from FY2025 OE and apply the post-expiration tax rate in the forecast.

audit_findings.title: Long-tail construction-defect costs could exceed the expense embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $155.1 million additional pre-tax expense under the filed 10% claim-frequency and cost sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse reserve development or weaker insurance recoveries would reduce future OE through higher construction-defect expense and cash payments.
audit_findings.evidence: A 10% increase in the claim frequency and the average cost per claim used to estimate the reserves would result in an increase of approximately $198.4 million in our reserves and a $43.3 million increase in our insurance receivable, resulting in additional expense of $155.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: No present under-reserving error is demonstrated. The company already records substantial reserves and related expense, while the finding concerns future claims development under subjective assumptions. The filed sensitivity is 6.1% of anchor OE and could matter if adverse experience becomes sustained, particularly because post-2021 exposures are almost exclusively self-insured.
audit_findings.action: Monitor claim-frequency and severity triangles by closing cohort, reserve additions versus payments, insurance recoveries and post-2021 self-insured experience; rerun normalized OE if adverse development emerges or the reserve sensitivity becomes a recurring expense.
